group: Normal operation – valid inputs, default config

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchema instance is returned; no exception is thrown.
cases.description: Verifies the happy‑path where a proper schema location, a valid JSON schema node and the default (null) configuration are supplied. The method should create a ValidationContext, delegate to doCreate, preload the schema and finally return a JsonSchema object.

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchema instance is returned; the ValidationContext inside the created schema must reflect the custom path type and fail‑fast flag.
cases.description: Ensures that a non‑null configuration is correctly passed to createValidationContext and that the resulting JsonSchema respects the supplied configuration (e.g., path type JSON‑Pointer and fail‑fast mode).

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or NullPointerException depending on implementation) thrown from getSchemaLocation or downstream processing.
cases.description: Tests the behaviour when the schema location argument is null. The factory should reject a null location early (via getSchemaLocation) and raise an appropriate exception.

cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown from createValidationContext (or a custom IllegalArgumentException).
cases.description: A null JsonNode does not represent a valid schema. The factory should detect this and fail before attempting to create a JsonSchema.

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchema instance is returned; preload() should be a no‑op because the config contains no special flags.
cases.description: Confirms that an explicitly created but otherwise default configuration does not alter the normal flow and that preload() does not attempt any extra loading.

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchema instance is returned; the internal doCreate call receives suppressSubSchemaRetrieval = false (as per method signature) but preload() respects the config and does not attempt to resolve the $ref.
cases.description: Ensures that when the configuration asks to suppress sub‑schema retrieval, the factory does not try to load referenced schemas during preload, avoiding unnecessary I/O or recursion.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException thrown from getSchemaLocation because the URI cannot be parsed.
cases.description: Ensures that a schema location containing a syntactically invalid URI is rejected early, preventing further processing.

group: Empty schemaUri string – should be treated as missing

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or NullPointerException) thrown because an empty location is not a valid schema identifier.
cases.description: Verifies that the factory does not accept an empty string as a schema location and fails fast.

group: Schema validation enabled – invalid schema should raise exception

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException (or ValidationException) thrown during preload because the schema is not compliant with the meta‑schema.
cases.description: When validation of the supplied schema is turned on, the factory must check the schema against its meta‑schema and reject an illegal "type" value.

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchema instance is returned; the ValidationContext inside the schema uses JSON_PATH as its path representation.
cases.description: Checks that a non‑default path type (JSON_PATH) is correctly propagated to the ValidationContext and reflected in error messages/paths.

group: Combined flags – failFast true and suppressSubSchemaRetrieval true

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchema instance is returned; preload does not attempt to resolve the $ref because suppression is active, and any validation failures would be reported immediately due to fail‑fast mode.
cases.description: Validates that the factory honours multiple configuration flags simultaneously without conflict.

group: Explicit default config – config object with all defaults set explicitly

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchema instance is returned; behavior is identical to passing null config.
cases.description: Ensures that providing a freshly instantiated config that has not been modified behaves the same as using the default (null) configuration.

group: SchemaNode is an empty object – should still produce a JsonSchema

cases.expected: A non‑null JsonSchema instance is returned; the schema represents an unrestricted schema (any JSON value is valid).
cases.description: Verifies that an empty JSON object, which is a valid (though unrestricted) schema, is accepted by the factory.

group: SchemaNode is a JSON array – not a valid schema root

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException (or IllegalArgumentException) thrown because the root of a schema must be an object, not an array.
cases.description: Ensures that the factory validates the structural requirement that a JSON Schema document must be a JSON object.

group: Primitive schemaNode root – not an object

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or JsonSchemaException) thrown because the schema root must be a JSON object, not a primitive value.
cases.description: Ensures that a schema supplied as a JSON primitive (string, number, boolean, or null) is rejected. The factory should detect that the root node is not an object and raise an appropriate exception before attempting to create a JsonSchema.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException thrown from getSchemaLocation because the URI scheme (ftp) is not supported by the factory.
cases.description: Verifies that the factory validates the scheme of the supplied SchemaLocation. Only supported schemes (e.g., http, https, classpath, file) should be accepted; an unsupported scheme must cause an early failure.

group: Config with null path type causing NullPointerException

cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown when constructing JsonNodePath because the path type resolved from the configuration is null.
cases.description: Tests the behaviour when a custom SchemaValidatorsConfig explicitly sets a null path type. The factory later calls validationContext.getConfig().getPathType() to build a JsonNodePath; a null value should result in a NullPointerException, confirming that the method does not silently accept an invalid configuration.
